name: MC33078 / MC33079 (NCV33078 / NCV33079)
tagline: Motorola's low-noise bipolar dual/quad (4.5 nV/√Hz, 16 MHz, 7 V/µs); Musiland chose it over the OP275 for its DACs.

lineage.note: Original 'DUAL/QUAD LOW NOISE OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS'; standalone MC33078/D Rev 0 dated 1996.
Motorola spin-off continuing the original design. MC33078/D Rev. 1 (2001) to Rev. 10 (2025); NCV added Rev. 9.
Own die (SLLS633), believed same as LM833; now shared with NE5532, LM833, RC4580 (E2E 2026).
SGS-Thomson copy survives. Specified 15 MHz GBP versus 16 MHz, suggesting its own die (unconfirmed).
Clone; datasheets reportedly on alldatasheet and datasheet4u. Unconfirmed.

onsemi automotive quad; Active and AEC-qualified.
TI SOIC-8; DigiKey 716887. Top mark reportedly 'M33078'.
TI VSSOP-8. Octopart files TI Rev. A under MC33078DGKR.
TI PDIP-8; TI part-details page exists.

In TI Rev. A title and a 2013 Soomal photo; no current TI page.
ST orderables; YDT probably automotive. Alldatasheet entries 23288 and 23289.
UTC version reportedly indexed on alldatasheet and datasheet4u; unconfirmed.

key_specs.value: ±5 V to ±18 V (36 V max VCC to VEE)

key_specs.condition: all amps, no load; ST about 4 mA

key_specs.value: 29 mA typ, 15 mA min; swing +14.1 / −14.6 V
0.15 mV typ, 2 mV max; drift 2 µV/°C typ
Bipolar (NPN vs PNP unconfirmed); CMRR 100 dB, Aol 800

reputation.summary: A budget low-noise part praised mainly by Soomal. Musiland dropped the OP275 for the MC33079 in its Monitor 03 US/PS (2011), then used it in the 06 MX, 10 and 06 Plus. Soomal heard better treble detail, finer resolution and slightly brighter sound, but judged whole products and called it not top-tier Hi-Fi. No ASR or Self measurements.
typical_uses: I/V for current-output DACs (Musiland PCM1798 cards)
Post-DAC filter and gain stage (Monitor 10, AK4490)
Preamps, filters, pedals; TL07x/NE5532 upgrade rolling
caveats: Needs at least ±5 V (10 V total); unsuitable for USB-bus designs without a boost converter.
Bipolar input with about 300 nA bias, so source impedances and DC paths matter.
TI's die differs from onsemi's and is now shared with NE5532, LM833, RC4580; same number, different silicon.
ST specifies 15 MHz versus 16 MHz; no cross-vendor listening or measurement comparison found.
Soomal praise is whole-product; reviews mislabel brands (an onsemi MC33079DG called 'Motorola').

counterfeit_notes: No specific counterfeit reports. Risk lies in unbranded lots (eBay '50/10 pcs MC33078DR SOP-8 MC33078D'). TI mark reportedly 'M33078'. Distrust 'Motorola' parts dated well after 2001, when ON-branded MC33078/D Rev. 1 appeared. Buy authorized; check logo and date code.

part_numbers_affected: MC33078D, MC33078P, MC33078DGKR, MC33078DGKT (other TI MC33078 orderables; covered by the E2E die-merge statement, PCN listing not seen)
silicon_changes.summary: TI unified the NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 dies, keeping part numbers (E2E 1652528). MC33078DR went through the Nov 2023 SFAB 150 mm → RFAB PCN with NE5532DR and LM833DR. MC33078 is probably the donor design; any circuit change unconfirmed. Hackaday (3 Jun 2026) and Headphonesty (Jul 2026) covered it.
silicon_changes.identification: No marker; datasheet still SLLS633C and no datasheet PCN. TI date codes from 2024 are probably new silicon. onsemi, ST, UTC and Motorola parts unaffected.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Probably small: SLLS633C still says 7 V/µs, 4.5 nV/√Hz. Large deltas (9→5 V/µs, diodes removed, ±22→±18 V) are NE5532's (SLOS075K).
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: pin-compatible, limits unchanged, but process migration confirmed; re-qualify new TI lots for overload or protection behaviour.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN listing of MC33078DR and E2E title confirmed; MC33078-level circuit change unconfirmed.

silicon_changes.vendor: Texas Instruments and STMicroelectronics vs onsemi (Motorola original design)
silicon_changes.summary: Same part number, different silicon. TI's die is believed identical to its LM833 (E2E 1443925) and is now the shared NE5532/LM833/RC4580 die. onsemi continues Motorola's design. ST's GBP spec differs, suggesting an independent die. No vendor-to-vendor comparison found.
silicon_changes.identification: Check logo and top mark (TI reportedly 'M33078'). ST gives 15 MHz GBP versus 16 MHz. TI's MC33079 appears only in its early Rev. A datasheet.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown; headline noise and slew match, but internal circuits may differ, so reviews may not carry across vendors.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: pinout and headline specs match; differences are second-order (GBW, possibly input protection).
silicon_changes.verification: ST MC33079 datasheet (15 MHz) and TI Rev. A found; 'MC33079 (TI)' removed as current part.

silicon_changes.summary: ON PCN 11528 (19 July 2001) moved devices from Motorola's BMC fab in Mesa, AZ to ON's Tesla fab in Roznov, Czech Republic. MC33078D/P listed; MC33079D/P reportedly. Untransferred BMC products went EOL under PCN 11785 (27 Sep 2001). Same original design.
silicon_changes.identification: No marking rule found. Pre-2001/2002 date codes likely Mesa wafers, later ones Roznov (inference).
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None documented; same design at another fab, no before/after comparison found.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same design and part numbers; only process spread within datasheet limits.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN 11528 and MC33078D/P listing confirmed; PCN 11785 confirmed as discontinuance. MC33079D/P not separately seen.

open_questions: onsemi: where are MC33078/D Revs 3, 6, 7? What did Rev. 10 change? Which revision is Mouser 1192984?

Does TI still sell an MC33079? Are the ST and UTC dies independent?

Capture current noise, output-swing conditions, and whether 29 mA is short-circuit current. Read diyAudio thread 344397.
